title: Elysian Energy — Model Acceptance Brief (pinned prompts, private slices, regression plan)
body:
Purpose:
This brief captures the minimal artifact set we require to accept an LLM model into Elysian Energy's production inference path. Contains the pinned prompt deck (golden prompts), a description of the private dataset slices for QA/regression, specific acceptance criteria (quality + perf), and the sign-off checklist for rollout. This is a working doc — expect iterative updates.

Scope and constraints:
- Customer: Elysian Energy (B2B energy analytics). Sensitive PII in private datasets — access restricted to eng-applied-ml and EE-secured-team.
- Target features: natural-language incident summarization, outage-impact estimation, and contract-extraction.
- Allowed model variants: FP16 and 4-bit quantized candidate builds with identical tokenizer. No architectural changes during acceptance run.
- Timebox: evaluation sprint = 2 weeks; regression window = last 30 production-like prompts.

Private dataset (controlled slices) — short descriptions (location + purpose):
1) ee_ops_incidents_2023_q4 (slice: high-severity incidents): 420 labeled incidents, fields: raw_log_snippet, human_summary, impact_score (0-10). Used for summarization P0 tests.
2) ee_customer_contracts_redacted (slice: redacted clauses): 300 doc pairs (raw contract, gold-extractions). Used for extraction recall/precision gating.
3) ee_telemetry_signal_summaries (synthetic-augmented): 1,200 pairs used for numeric interpretation and outage candidate ranking.
4) ee_privacy_smoke_tests (small, fuzzed): 50 examples designed to probe PII leakage.
Notes: datasets are stored in internal S3 bucket s3://redwood-private/elysian/ and access-controlled. DO NOT export outside VPC.

Pinned prompt deck (golden set) — do not change without approval. These are the canonical evaluation prompts used in automatic scoring and manual sign-off: 
- P1: "Summarize the following incident log for the on-call engineer in <= 3 sentences and state the likely root cause." (Expected: concise summary + root cause label)
- P2: "From the contract excerpt below, list all termination clauses and their effective notice periods in JSON array format." (Expected: array with clause title and days)
- P3: "Given telemetry series A,B,C describe in bullet form which signal indicates immediate outage and why." (Expected: identify series and short justification)
- P4: "Redact any customer-identifying information from the text and return only the sanitized content." (Expected: no PII artifacts remain)
- P5: "Rate the incident's customer-impact on a 0-10 scale and supply one sentence recommending next action."
Each pinned prompt has an associated scoring rubric in the test harness. See linked_artifacts for test repo.

Evaluation methodology and metrics:
- Automatic metrics: ROUGE-L / token-level exact-match for extraction tasks; BLEU not used. For summarization we use ROUGE-L and a proprietary semantic-similarity score (SSS) computed by the eval harness. For classification/impact scoring use mean absolute error (MAE) against human impact_score.
- Human review: 3 annotators for a 150-sample sign-off slate; majority vote to flag regressions. Annotator instructions under confluence: see ELY-ENERGY-ANNOTATOR-GUIDE.
- Perf metrics: p95 latency (cold start excluded) and tokens/sec throughput observed under a 10 QPS synthetic workload. SLOs defined below.

Acceptance criteria (hard gates):
Quality gates (must all pass):
- Summarization: SSS >= 0.78 on ee_ops_incidents_2023_q4 test slice AND ROUGE-L >= 0.45.
- Extraction (contracts): exact-match F1 >= 0.82 on ee_customer_contracts_redacted.
- Numeric/outage ranking: Top-1 accuracy >= 0.88 on telemetry test slice.
- PII: ee_privacy_smoke_tests must show zero PII leaks on automated detector + no redaction failures in manual sample of 20.
- Human sign-off: the 150-sample manual slate must have <= 5% critical regressions (critical = incorrect root cause or missed termination clause).

Performance gates (must all pass):
- Latency: p95 <= 420ms for generation up to 256 tokens under dedicated candidate serving config (batching advisory applied).
- Throughput: achieves >= 70 tokens/sec sustained per endpoint under 10 QPS synthetic load.
- Mem/CPU: KV cache warm memory footprint must not exceed 18GB for the candidate quantized variant.

Regression tests to run (automated harness):
- nightly-regression (full suite) — runs on new model build; compare to baseline model (current production) using delta thresholds: quality metric drop < 2% absolute for primary metrics.
- smoke-fast (subset) — P1,P2,P4 pinned prompts across private slices; run after any code change in tokenization path.
- adversarial-noise (fuzzed) — run on telemetry and incidents with injected typos to validate resilience.
- privacy-probe — executes ee_privacy_smoke_tests and runs leakage detector.
Test outputs: per-example logs, token-level diffs, scoring artifacts. Harness writes run artifacts to gs://redwood-evals/elysian/runs/<date>/ and creates a summarized JSON report at github:repo/elysian-energy/acceptance-tests/actions.

Manual sign-off process (roles + checklist):
Approvers required:
- Applied ML lead: Priya Desai (owner)
- Customer success technical lead: Marco Ruiz
- Security reviewer: Liang Chen
- Product owner (Elysian): Ava Thompson
Sign-off checklist (all items must be checked):
- [ ] Automated suite green (nightly-regression; delta < 2% vs baseline)
- [ ] Human 150-sample slate reviewed; critical regressions <= 5%
- [ ] Latency and throughput SLOs met in dedicated test environment
- [ ] Privacy probe passed (no PII leakage)
- [ ] Deployment runbook reviewed and rollback tested (playbook id: EE-DR-42)
- [ ] Canary plan approved (canary size, duration, error thresholds)
- [ ] Customer notified and scheduled for deployment window
Sign-off format: each approver posts a comment in the PR that references the summarized run JSON (artifact link) and sets the GitHub PR approval. Final merge by Applied ML lead.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Canary (5% of traffic) for 24 hours with real-time observability (console dashboard: model/elysian/canary). Auto-fallback to baseline on error rate spike > 2x baseline.
2) Gradual ramp to 100% over 3 days if canary stable.
3) Post-rollout 72-hour observation with increased sampling for human checks.

Open questions / TODOs:
- TODO: finalize annotator compensation for manual slate (Marco)
- Q: Do we require a separate privacy review from Legal for synthetic telemetry augmentation? (Assigned: Liang)
- TODO: add a failover variant (cheaper quantized) to the smart-routing policy if throughput dips (owner: platform-eng).

Notes to reviewers:
- This brief intentionally defines conservative gates for first production integration. We expect relaxation after the first two successful rollouts.
- If a metric narrowly misses (within 0.5% absolute) reach out in #eng-applied-ml before failing the gate; a one-time exception can be recorded but must be documented in the run JSON and approved by the four approvers above.

History / changelog:
- 2024-10-14: initial draft by Priya Desai
- 2024-11-01: added privacy probe and pinned prompt P4 (Liang Chen)
- 2024-12-12: updated SSS thresholds after bench re-run (Marco Ruiz)
- 2025-01-22: consolidated sign-off checklist and added rollout steps (final revision before customer review)

Contact + access:
- Primary author: Priya Desai (priya@redwood.com)
- Slack: #eng-applied-ml (tag @priya for questions)
- Dataset S3 path: s3://redwood-private/elysian/ (request access via IAM ticket EE-DATA-ACCESS)

End of brief.
